background_notes.fact: For real q<=r, the identity on Fourier coefficients defines a continuous inclusion H^r into H^q of norm at most one. Mean-zero Fourier truncations converge in H^r to every mean-zero H^r element.

grounds.reason: The H^s norms and completions are defined by weighted square sums.
The actual endpoint use has q=epsP<=1/8=r; S004 also uses a_gamma<=1+gamma.

background_notes.justification: Since 1+k^2>=1, the q-weight is bounded by the r-weight term by term. Summing and taking square roots proves the contraction on polynomials and hence on the completions. The tail of the defining convergent nonnegative series tends to zero, proving truncation convergence. Setting the zero coefficient to zero preserves mean zero. For nonnegative q,r these inclusions identify the same L2 function.

background_notes.fact: S_a is an isometric linear bijection on every H^q, preserves the mean, and has group law S_(a+r)=S_a S_r. On smooth inputs Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=S_(-a)Fstage_(0,t-a)(S_a f,S_a g).

grounds.reason: B is defined in terms of S and the spatial derivative.
Fstage is half the time integral of B.
The smooth covariance and affine integration substitution are used here.

background_notes.justification: The multiplier has modulus one and is one at zero; scalar exponential multiplication proves the group law, and S_(-a) is the inverse. Insert this law in B_(a+r), then substitute s=a+r in the smooth compact-interval integral. A bounded linear map commutes with this integral, as follows already from its Riemann sums in any fixed Sobolev space. This gives exactly the stated covariance.

background_notes.fact: A continuous path which is smooth in space and C1 on each closed piece of a finite compact time partition has weak time derivative equal almost everywhere to its piecewise derivative, with bounded L2 path norm and bounded H^(-23/14) derivative norm.

grounds.reason: X uses weak derivative and essential suprema.
This is the specified initial path domain.
The finite partition, compactness, smoothness and continuity used at A001 are explicitly stated.

background_notes.justification: Continuity on the finitely many compact pieces bounds the relevant path and derivative norms. Integrate against a compactly supported scalar test function and integrate by parts separately on each piece. The adjacent endpoint values agree, so all internal boundary terms cancel. Thus the piecewise derivative is the weak derivative, with no point masses.

background_notes.fact: A multilinear map on dense input subspaces with a product norm bound into a complete normed target has a unique continuous extension to their norm closures, with the same bound. This applies to the displayed constant-input Ctri and bilinear stage estimates and to the stated initial path-domain closure in X. Identities between such maps persist on these completions.

background_notes.justification: Expand a difference of outputs by replacing one input at a time. Each term is bounded by one input difference times the remaining bounded input norms, so approximating outputs are Cauchy and their limits are independent of approximants. The same expansion proves continuity and preserves the bound and multilinearity. For paths, ||z||_(L-infinity H^(-pstar))<=||z||_(L-infinity L2)<=||z||_X by the Fourier weights, so E003 also gives a controlling product-X bound. No density in the full X space is assumed. For the stage identities use the same mean-zero Fourier truncations and the bounded S maps; continuous inclusion H^(1+gamma) into H^(a_gamma) ensures the two target limits coincide as distributions.
